confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on one web search of 2026 cost-of-living summaries for London. They include Expatica, which quotes Numbeo data from June 2026, plus Moneyfarm and MyLifeElsewhere. Sterling averages from those sources were: about £7.08 for a pint of beer, £4.11-£4.29 for a cappuccino, about £20 for an inexpensive meal and about £81 for a three-course meal for two. I converted these at roughly 1.35 USD per GBP. That rate comes from my general knowledge and the GBP/USD pairs shown by MyLifeElsewhere, not from an official source. The cocktail (about £14) and wine-glass (about £9) prices were not directly checked. I estimated them from general knowledge of London prices and their usual relationship to beer prices. All four accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates and were not checked against live listings or searches. London accommodation prices in July are high-season prices and vary a lot by area, so these figures are the least certain. The FX observation comes from a search summary citing the RBA rate of 0.6720 for 18 November 2026. The source URL is the RBA exchange-rates page shown in the search results; I did not read that page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food and drink prices come from London-specific 2026 aggregates. Accommodation is benchmarked against London's usual position as one of Europe's most expensive peak-season cities, at a similar or higher level than Paris and Amsterdam.
